sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the proof from the obligation for a husband to visit his wife before a journey shows that the unification (Pekidah) occurred even during the time of the Temple's pledging, as seen in the cherubim embracing during the destruction.

translations.translation: And one may add,

that this which [the Alter Rebbe] brings in Likkutei Torah as a proof that the unification is called "Pekidah" from that which our sages of blessed memory said, "A man is obligated to visit his wife,"
is,
because this statement of our sages of blessed memory speaks of the obligation to visit his wife at the time when he is going out on a journey,
and in this it hints,
that in addition to the matter of the "Pekudei HaMishkan" (the accountings of the Tabernacle),
that the intention in this—that the Sanctuary was pledged—is in order that through repentance there will be afterward
(in the future to come)
the unification
(Pekidah)
in a more elevated manner,
even during this very time itself
(when the Sanctuary was pledged)
there was the unification.
And as is explained elsewhere,
what our sages of blessed memory said,
"At the time when the gentiles entered the Sanctuary, they saw the cherubim intertwined with each other,"
for this is seemingly perplexing,
for cherubim intertwined with each other indicates the greatness of the affection of the Holy One, blessed be He, and Israel, like the affection of a man and a woman,
and at the time when the gentiles entered the Sanctuary, it was seemingly the opposite of affection.
And the explanation of this is,
that since during the time of exile the Congregation of Israel is like a woman whose husband has gone to a country overseas,
therefore,
before the departure of the husband
(the Holy One, blessed be He)
on the journey,
there was the "Pekidah" (visitation/unification),
and therefore the cherubim were then like the embracing
of a man and his wife.
However, the Pekidah that took place then was in concealment,
and in revelation there was the destruction and the exile,
and the intention in this is that through the service during the time of exile,
and particularly through the service of repentance,
the Pekidah will be revealed in the building of the Third Holy Temple,
and then the pledge will also be returned,
the Mishkan and the Mishkan of Testimony,
with the coming of Mashiach Tzidkeinu, speedily and truly.
